focus.jbig: Oil crashes on Iran peace talks · tape steadies after Friday’s AI rout · midterms Tue · 3 setups boarded
focus.jtag: Crude tumbled ~3–4% as Iran–Qatar diplomacy eased war fears, lifting risk sentiment; futures firmed after Friday’s 1.82% S&P drop. The scanner boarded CHKP (Type A, bearish) plus IBB and MO (Type C, bullish breakouts)
focus.jnote: The backdrop improved over the weekend — but it’s not an all-clear. The S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,580.07 on Friday — its worst session since June — from a prior close of 7,720.39. This morning risk steadied: US equity futures rose as falling oil prices buoyed sentiment, with Nasdaq-100 contracts up 0.6% and S&P 500 futures up 0.3%. The big mover is crude — global oil prices fell more than 3% as Iranian and Qatari officials negotiated an end to the US–Israeli war on Iran, with WTI dropping to ~$100.69 and Brent to ~$109.75. The VIX, though, is still bid: it sits at 19.42 with the S&P at 7,580, after touching 23.93 during Friday’s sell-off. And the week is front-loaded with events: Apple and Palantir report after the close today, the midterms and an RBA decision land Tuesday, and US payrolls come Friday. Calmer, yes — but not the clean, quiet tape a Sniper wants to sell premium into.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the two breakouts (IBB and MO) are the cleanest technically. IBB is trading near its 52-week high of $222.29 and held above its $216.96 pivot on ~1.8x volume — biotech/health care has been a defensive-rotation beneficiary as the AI trade wobbles. MO (Altria) held above its $76.07 pivot on ~1.6x volume, a low-beta tobacco staple that tends to steady a risk-off tape. Both passed the scanner’s liquidity gate. But on a RED day with the VIX near 19.4 and a midterm/earnings gauntlet ahead, both are watch-only — one-session-old breakouts fail easily when headlines whip the tape.
focus.notup: One bearish name boarded — CHKP, a post-earnings gap down. Check Point’s Q3 revenue missed consensus by 2.3%, EPS was in line, and shares fell ~6.6% premarket as investors focused on top-line weakness. But the gap printed on near-zero relative volume (0.02x), far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, and the CEO told investors revenue bottomed this quarter and should improve gradually from Q4 — a forward signal that cuts against the bearish gap. Selling a bear call into that squeeze setup on a RED day invites trouble. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? P(≥1% gap) at ~38% is above the 35% trigger — that alone locks out GREEN — and composite ~57 sits in WARM. The oil crash genuinely eased the geopolitical tail, but the VIX is still ~19.4 after Friday’s AI rout, and this week stacks tomorrow’s midterm elections, tonight’s Apple/Palantir prints, and Friday’s payrolls — three unscheduled-outcome catalysts in a row. Every boarded Type A/C name is either volume-unconfirmed (CHKP) or a one-session-old breakout (IBB, MO). Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the event cluster and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Boarded Type A, graded A, bearish — a revenue-miss gap down, but a conflicted one with no volume behind it. Check Point’s Q3 revenue missed consensus by 2.3%, EPS was in line, and shares fell ~6.6% premarket to ~$142.51 from the $152.11 close — a realized gap (~−6.3%) smaller than the ~9.9% options-implied move. The catch: CEO Nadav Zafrir told investors revenue bottomed this quarter and should improve gradually beginning in Q4, a forward signal that undercuts the bearish thesis. Scanner flags: relative volume 0.02x is far below the 1.3x bar (no participation confirmation), and 2 S/R layers sit just overhead (sma20 $142.88, gap floor $152.11). OI OK (~2,674). Watch-only on a RED day. Next earnings ~Feb 1, 2027.
setups.check_note: Don’t open new premium on a RED day — and respect the squeeze risk. The gap is bearish on a revenue miss, but an in-line EPS and an explicit “revenue has troughed” call from the CEO create real reclaim risk, and a ~6% gap on 0.02x volume is unconfirmed. For a bear call, confirm at 9:35 that price < prior close ($152.11) AND < open AND lower third of range. Liquidity NOT verified — confirm ATM spread and OI on the platform before entry.

setups.read: Boarded Type C, graded A, bullish — a held breakout on real volume, the cleanest technical name on the board. IBB is trading near its 52-week high of $222.29, holding ~$218.10 above its $216.96 pivot (extended just ~0.5%) after a breakout that has now held 1 session — stronger than a same-day pop. Breakout-day volume ran ~1.8x the 50-day average, clearing the 1.3x bar, and biotech/health care has been a defensive-rotation beneficiary as the AI trade wobbles. Liquidity passed: ATM spread $0.80 (bar $1.10), OI ~1,511 on the Nov-20 $220 chain. One hard gate: next earnings date is UNKNOWN — as an ETF there’s no single-name print, but verify the heavy holdings’ calendars (Vertex, Amgen, Gilead, Regeneron) before entry. Watch-only on a RED day.

The ~1.8x volume and the held pivot are the best structure on the board, and biotech’s defensive bid is a genuine tailwind, but headline whips (Apple/Palantir tonight, midterms Tue) can snap a young breakout. If taken later, confirm at 9:35 that price > the $216.96 pivot AND > open AND holding the upper third of range; half size. Verify the top holdings’ earnings dates first.

Breakout-day volume ran ~1.6x the 50-day average, clearing the 1.3x bar, and a tobacco staple with a steady dividend tends to hold up when risk assets wobble. risks: Apple & Palantir tonight — both report after the US close today; on the heels of Friday’s AI-capex rout, a soft mega-cap read can re-crack the whole index. Keep every spread clear of its name’s print.
Midterm elections Tuesday — results will shape Congress’s spending plans and priorities; an uncertain or contested outcome is an unscheduled gap catalyst stacked right on top of earnings.

Iran diplomacy is two-sided — the oil crash is built on hope: future price moves depend on the negotiations and the risk of renewed military escalation, and the threat of a broader conflict still supports crude. A talks breakdown reverses it fast.
Payrolls Friday — US payrolls land Friday; a hot or cold jobs number can whip rates and risk into the weekend, the kind of scheduled event a 7-DTE spread must clear.

Vol still elevated & credit cracking — the VIX sits ~19.4 after touching ~24 Friday, and US high-yield spreads widened 17 bps Friday to a new nearly 18-month high of 340 bps — stress is seeping beyond equities.
